title: "How to use this course"
toc: true
---

## Who it's for

Developers and ML practitioners who want to go beyond surface-level API usage and genuinely
understand how modern AI systems work — and how to build, adapt, and ship them. Comfort with
Python is assumed; the necessary math and deep-learning fundamentals are covered along the way.

## The daily rhythm

One tutorial per day, ~30 minutes. Each one is self-contained but builds on the last, so work
through them in order. Don't just read — run the code and attempt the exercises.

## Anatomy of every tutorial

Every tutorial follows the same structure, so you always know where to find things:

1. **In this tutorial** — a short intro: what you'll learn, why it matters, and prerequisites.
2. **Concepts** — the core ideas, with diagrams and formulas where they help.
3. **Worked example** — runnable Python you can follow along with.
4. **Key takeaways** — the few things to remember.
5. **Check your understanding** — 5 control questions with reveal-able answers.
6. **Coding tasks** — 2 Python exercises, each openable in Google Colab, with solutions.
7. **References** — where to go deeper.

## Running the code

Two ways to run the hands-on parts:

- **Google Colab (recommended for GPU work).** The coding tasks in each tutorial have an
  **Open in Colab** badge. Colab gives you a free GPU — important for the fine-tuning,
  quantization, and serving sections.
- **Locally.** Clone the repo and use [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/amhellmund/ai-engineering-in-100-days.git
  cd ai-engineering-in-100-days
  uv sync
  ```

  Then run a notebook with `uv run jupyter lab` (lightweight tutorials run fine on CPU).

## A note on the content

Tutorials are drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by a human before publishing. A tutorial
still marked **draft** may change. Found an error? Open an issue on
[GitHub](https://github.com/amhellmund/ai-engineering-in-100-days).
